{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The bell did not ring until past two, and when it did it was not her. It was Halloran from the mill, wanting washers, and he stood at the counter with his big hands spread on the wood on either side of the card and never once looked down at it. He talked about the weather and the price of feed and a cousin in Limerick who had done well for himself, and all the while the card lay there between his thumbs like a thing that had always been there and would always be. When he left, the door swung slow behind him and the light shifted on the floor.

After that a long quiet. He swept though the floor did not need it. He straightened the boxes of screws by size and then by finish and then back by size. He did not pick up the card. He had decided about that, and a decision, once made in that shop, was a nail driven.

Near four the shadow of the awning had crossed the whole of the front step and begun on the road. He heard footsteps that were hers before he saw her, because he had been hearing them for thirty years in the way a man hears his own name in a crowd. She stopped at the door. She did not come in. She looked past him to the counter, to the small white rectangle on it, and something in her face let go, a rope paid out.

"You've left it there," she said.

"I have."

She nodded once, as though a sum had come right, and stepped over the threshold."}
